title: PRD update: regression escape-hatch, runbook-driven acceptance criteria, and observability ownership
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: After the recent degraded-serving incident that impacted tail latency and caused automatic fallback to a lower-quality model variant, translate postmortem action items into explicit PRD changes. This ticket updates the serving PRD to add a formal 'regression escape hatch' (manual and automated rollback paths), explicit observability ownership, SLO-triggered acceptance gates, and end-to-end verification requirements. The goal is to ensure future regressions are detectable earlier, have documented remediation paths, and ship with verifiable acceptance criteria and ownership for on-call and release engineers.
acceptance_criteria: PRD contains a documented regression escape-hatch that defines both an automated rollback and a manual operator 'panic rollback' with exact steps, required permissions, and expected post-rollback verification checklist.

SLO triggers are specified: service error-rate increase > 3x baseline sustained for 2 minutes OR p99 latency > 3x baseline sustained for 5 minutes must open a high-priority incident and execute the automated escape-hatch unless overridden by the on-call lead.

Observability ownership is assigned: a named team and on-call rotation must own the key dashboards (latency distribution, error classes, model fallback rate, cache-regen rate, request-size distribution) and runbook maintenance.

Dashboards and alerts: required Grafana dashboard panels and PagerDuty alert definitions are listed in the PRD with links; alert noise-reduction rules (suppression windows, dynamic baselines) are documented.

Release gating: any rollout touching runtime kernels, batching logic, or KV-cache heuristics requires synthetic canary runs (traffic shadowing) and a pass on the regression checklist before 50% traffic ramp.

Acceptance tests: automated canary scenarios and chaos-simulated degradation tests are added to the verification harness and must pass in staging before GA rollout; test definitions and expected metrics are in PRD.
Operator documentation: a concise runbook section with escape-hatch play, rollback command examples (CLI/Console), and post-rollback diagnostics is embedded and linked to the company runbook library.
Security review: changes that alter rollback primitives or control-plane permissions have an explicit security review sign-off recorded in the PRD.
Post-release monitoring: a two-week post-rollout monitoring checklist with thresholds for auto rollback, and an owner for weekly regression reports is defined.
notes: Supporting artifacts: postmortem (https://confluence.redwood.com/pm/postmortem/2026-degraded-serving), initial incident timeline spreadsheet, and the ops incident runbook draft. Related PRs: runtime kernel change proposal (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4521) and KV-cache heuristics refactor PR (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4589). Stakeholders: Runtime, SRE, Observability, Product. Meetings held: 2026-03-05 incident debrief, 2026-03-09 cross-functional PRD alignment workshop. Proposed rollout plan and verification schedule included as attachments in the PRD page.
